comment: Everything the build is allowed to fetch, pinned. A build that resolves a
version at build time is a build whose output nobody can reproduce, and a
signed binary has to be reproducible from the commit the release records.
Move a pin deliberately, in its own commit, with the reason.

lkl.why: The ext4 the drives are formatted with needs a kernel of 5.15 or newer for orphan_file; this is the LKL tree we found and fixed the three flush faults against (docs/0c-step1-flush-proof.md).

headers.comment: Where each header lives in Dokany's tree, and where the build wants it. They include each other by plain name, so they go flat into vendor/include and one -I covers all three.

dokany.why: Its dokan2.sys is signed by the Microsoft Windows Hardware Compatibility Publisher, which is what removes any need for an extended-validation certificate. Verified in docs/dokany-verification.md.
dokany.note: The headers are not in the installer and are taken from the tag. dokan2.dll comes from the installed SDK.

msys2.why: LKL builds natively under MSYS2; both cross-builds from Linux fail (x86_64 on LLP64 long, i686 crashes in lkl_start_kernel). See docs/0c-step1-flush-proof.md.
